argument_summary: The strongest supportable position is not clean compliance but caveated compliance: the admissible record supports certification of a controlled, reversible 5% rollout because aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and monitoring plus rollback reduce operational exposure, while the unresolved mental-health-referral-routing weakness is explicitly disclosed as a named limitation in the model card. The audit concern is correct that rollout controls do not by themselves satisfy the missing exclusion-or-risk-acceptance predicate. The narrower point is that the policy text shown here establishes a disclosure obligation for an exposed material limitation; it does not expressly make certification impossible when the limitation is disclosed and the launch is bounded and reversible.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated certification avoids treating the record as cleaner than it is, while also avoiding unnecessary escalation where the remaining issue can be bounded through explicit disclosure, staged exposure, rollback capability, and monitoring already in the packet.
claims_about_policy: The policy should not be read as saying rollout controls alone cure the weakness; they do not. The admissible evidence also does not show use-case exclusion or approved risk acceptance for the exposed mental health referral routing segment, so this is not a basis for claiming full mitigation. But the release-policy note says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the present record, the compliant path is therefore certification with explicit model-card disclosure of the unresolved limitation, not certification on a theory that the weakness has been eliminated.
concessions: The mental health referral routing segment remains below target and exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The admissible record does not show approved risk acceptance specifically covering that exposed segment.
Rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring do not by themselves satisfy the exclusion-or-risk-acceptance condition mentioned in the policy text.
This should not be characterized as uncaveated or fully mitigated compliance.
